title: Comparing cards with different reward currencies
notice: Synthetic and illustrative. Card names, facts and identifiers are invented. Arguments follow the server's input schemas; results show only some of the fields the server returns.
demonstrates: The assistant gives the request-history notice before the first Rewardopedia call.
A comparison keeps the requested order and reports whether it is complete.
Miles and cash back are not treated as equal money, and no overall winner is declared.
An unreported fee is described as unknown, not as zero.

steps.text: Compare the Example Travel Card and the Example Cash Card for me.

Before I use Rewardopedia: it keeps a sanitized history of each Rewardopedia request, including searches and comparisons, in your Rewardopedia account until you delete it. It saves facts you tell me, such as cards you hold, but I won't save anything you ask me not to. Both are shared across assistants connected to your account, and you can ask what is saved or ask me to forget it at any time. Please don't share card or account numbers.

Example Travel Card: $250 annual fee; earns 2 Example Miles per $1 on travel booked directly with airlines; Rewardopedia has no foreign transaction fee on record for it, so that fee is unknown. Example Cash Card: no annual fee; 1.5% cash back on everything; 3% foreign transaction fee. Miles and cash back are different currencies, so the 2x and 1.5% figures can't be compared directly, and neither card is better overall. If you travel abroad often, the unknown foreign transaction fee on the travel card is worth checking with the issuer first.
